alignments.note: Greek anarthrous; supplied The is a rule 7/51 helper on the noun it determines.
Rule 9: lexical verb heads over the supplied subject.

Rule 51: the ASV recasts the articular phrase as a predicate nominal and the article surfaces as the supplied indefinite, as JHN.6.60 does; the corpus aligns an article to a supplied 'a' in all 8 such units and never gives that determiner to a noun standing behind its own article (rules 31, 51, 57). REV.1.5 is the same construction with the definite.

REV.1.5's ho martys -> '*who is* the faithful witness' is this construction: the article takes only its determiner and the appositional predicate noun carries the supplied relativizer and copula, as EPH.6.9's kyrios -> 'who is Master', TIT.1.6 and 1PE.1.1 do, and as rule 68's koinonos -> 'he is partner' at 2CO.8.23 does for that very lexeme. Rule 31's carve-out is for a modifier with nothing to carry the relativizer; an expressed predicate noun carries it. Discontinuous under rule 15.
Anarthrous; supplied a is a rule 51 helper on the noun.
Rule 21: of the is one unit on the article; rule 57 keeps it on its own noun across the interposed genitive.
Rule 23: article before a name has no English realization.
Rule 17: of + noun heads on the noun.
